description: A field that receives a typed secret shows dots for the life of the page (ADR 01178): -webkit-text-security: disc, or a transparent color where the browser lacks it. A public variable and literal text stay visible. Each check also compares the field with the literal typed text, so the field still holds the real value. Safari runs on macOS only.

tests.description: A secret-named variable typed into a field hides the field text.

runBrowserScript.script: const el = document.querySelector('#text-input'); const s = getComputedStyle(el); const hidden = s.getPropertyValue('-webkit-text-security') === 'disc' || s.color === 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)'; return String(hidden) + ':' + String(el.value === 'typed-secret-8642');

tests.description: Safari, which has no headless mode, hides a typed secret the same way. macOS only.

runBrowserScript.script: const el = document.querySelector('#text-input'); const s = getComputedStyle(el); const hidden = s.getPropertyValue('-webkit-text-security') === 'disc' || s.color === 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)'; return String(hidden) + ':' + String(el.value === 'typed-secret-8642');

tests.description: A variable listed in publicVariables isn't secret, so the field text stays visible.

runBrowserScript.script: const el = document.querySelector('#text-input'); const s = getComputedStyle(el); const hidden = s.getPropertyValue('-webkit-text-security') === 'disc' || s.color === 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)'; return String(hidden) + ':' + String(el.value === 'public-text-1357');

tests.description: Text that came from no variable stays visible.

runBrowserScript.script: const el = document.querySelector('#text-input'); const s = getComputedStyle(el); const hidden = s.getPropertyValue('-webkit-text-security') === 'disc' || s.color === 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)'; return String(hidden) + ':' + String(el.value === 'kittens');
